answer: A new agent also needs sponsorship from three existing peers who vouch with their own stake, forming a comet-like trail of verifiable trust. Each agent must stake tokens and maintain a unique hardware pulse beacon tied to its island node, making duplicate identities costly to fake. An attacker must fund, register, and sustain many real devices plus recruit colluding sponsors, so the cost of creating N sybils exceeds N times the stake plus hardware and reputation loss, making mass fakery economically irrational. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
